instructions: Cut the carrots, celery and potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces, dice the onion, and mince the garlic. Small pieces are what get this on the table in time.
Set a large pot over medium-high heat and add the olive oil. Add the turkey and a pinch of salt. Break it up and cook for 5 minutes, letting it sit between stirs so it browns, until no pink is left.
Add the carrots, celery and onion. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until you can smell it.
Add 3 tbsp of the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens a shade.

Pour in the broth and the diced tomatoes with their juice, and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot. Add the potatoes, 1 cup of the corn, 1 cup of the green beans, the thyme, oregano and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to a steady simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, until a potato piece is tender when you pierce it.
Take out the bay leaf. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt and the pepper.
method_notes: Dear Crissy leads (4.45 from 438 ratings): brown the turkey, soften carrot, celery and onion, add garlic, then tomatoes, tomato paste, broth, potatoes, corn, green beans and herbs and simmer. The original makes 8 servings and simmers 30 to 35 minutes with a 1 hour total, so this halves the vegetables and broth, cuts everything to 1/2-inch pieces, and simmers 15 minutes to fit 45 minutes. Recipe Girl's version is faster (40 minutes) but uses kidney beans and cheese, so only its order of steps was a check. Frozen corn and green beans replace the canned ones to save draining.
